description: The weak-vertex trace's normalisation is the Jones-Markov relation: tr_M(closure of beta) = q^(2e)*V(q^-2)/[2]_q^(n-1), verified against the canonical engine on eight torus knots at n = 2,3,4,5. For T(3,5) this gives W = q^20*V(q^-2)/[2]_q^2, so the canonically-normalised coupling is J - 1 with J = V(q^-2) — no free constant, because V(1) = 1 and V'(1) = 0 for every knot. It factors as J - 1 = -h_4*h_6/q^10, a product of two q-differences at the two Jones exponents, which is why it vanishes to second order with leading coefficient -(2*4)(2*6) = -96. The beta-decay coupling is the same shape at half scale, s^2 = h_(1/2)^2, leading coefficient 1. So the leading ratio is exactly -96, which derives the ORDER of the 1.19e4 substitution factor of qou-ix74 (96^2 = 9216) while confirming no constant relates them: the ratio runs to -37.09 at q0.

convention.anchor: proton pin (Q_50_DIGIT_STR); identities exact in q

decay_coupling.honest_limit: a Jones exponent is an integer, so s^2 is a FORMAL half-scale analogue and not itself any knot's V - 1

order_of_substitution_factor.withdrawn_claim: the ORDER of the substitution factor is derived: 96**2 = 9216 against |W|**2/s**4 = 11875.44
order_of_substitution_factor.why_it_fails: |W|**2/s**k diverges as q->1 for every k >= 1 (W(1) = 1/4 != 0, s**2(1) = 0), so there is no leading constant; -96 is the leading value of (J-1)/s**2, a DIFFERENT ratio whose numerator vanishes because V_K(1) = 1 for every knot
order_of_substitution_factor.and_the_power_was_wrong: the rate carries s**2 once (prf:trace-ratio-observable), so the factor is 129.405107404, not 11875.4418936763
order_of_substitution_factor.what_survives: every exact identity in this witness: the Jones-Markov relation on eight torus knots, J - 1 = -h_4*h_6/q**10, the cyclotomic ratio -G_8*G_12/q**19, and its classical value -96

scope: POSITIVE derivation of the normalisation (the framing and rank factors are read off the braid word; the offset and vanishing order of J - 1 are topological). It does NOT derive the order of the decay-rate substitution factor -- that claim is retracted, see order_of_substitution_factor. NOT a rescaling constant — the ratio provably runs, consistent with the scope-(b) exclusion in qou-pfh7.

assertions.name: normalisation_rule_holds_on_eight_torus_knots
assertions.note: tr_M(closure) = q^(2e)*V(q^-2)/[2]_q^(n-1) verified against markov_trace_canonical for n = 2,3,4,5 incl. mirror pairs

assertions.name: every_jones_has_V_one_equals_one_and_V_prime_one_zero
assertions.note: the offset and the vanishing order of J - 1 are topological, not chosen — this is what fixes the normalisation

assertions.name: jones_deviation_is_product_of_two_q_differences
assertions.note: J - 1 = -h_4*h_6/q^10 exactly; exponents 4 and 6 are the Jones exponents of T(3,5), q^-10 is the framing

assertions.name: q_difference_derivative_at_one_is_two_k
assertions.note: h_k'(1) = 2k, so a product of two of them vanishes to second order with leading coefficient (2k1)(2k2)

assertions.name: jones_deviation_is_polynomial_after_framing
assertions.note: q^20*(J-1) = -(q^8-1)(q^12-1): the same fact with no negative powers, and the form the (q-1)^2 factor is read off

assertions.name: ratio_has_exact_cyclotomic_closed_form
assertions.note: q^19*(J-1) = -s^2*G_8*G_12, so (J-1)/s^2 = -G_8*G_12/q^19 EXACTLY — the ratio and its running, with no limit taken

assertions.name: cyclotomic_cofactors_at_one_are_the_jones_exponents
assertions.note: G_8(1) = 8, G_12(1) = 12, so the ratio at q = 1 is -8*12 = -96 — the Jones exponents themselves, doubled by h_k'(1) = 2k

assertions.name: leading_ratio_is_minus_ninety_six_but_ratio_runs
assertions.note: (J-1)/s^2 -> -96 at q=1 and -37.09 at q0: the framing q^-10 suppresses it, so no CONSTANT relates the two couplings (consistent with the qou-pfh7 exclusion, and explains it)

assertions.name: order_claim_retracted_substitution_factor_diverges
assertions.note: RETRACTED (bean qou-xql6): this producer claimed the ORDER of the substitution factor was derived, 96^2 = 9216 against |W|^2/s^4 = 11875. |W|^2/s^k DIVERGES as q->1 for k >= 1 because W(1) = 1/4 != 0, so it has no leading constant; -96 is the leading value of (J-1)/s^2, whose numerator vanishes since V_K(1) = 1 for every knot. Two different ratios. Also the power was s^2, not s^4, so the factor is 129.405107404
